candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS LHV Group’s consolidated net profit was EUR 24.7 million in Q2 2026, up 25% from EUR 19.7 million in Q1 but down 20% from EUR 30.8 million in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Profit attributable to the parent’s shareholders was EUR 24.1 million, compared with EUR 19.8 million and EUR 30.0 million in the respective comparison periods.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Earnings per share rose to EUR 0.07 from EUR 0.06 quarter on quarter but declined from EUR 0.09 year on year.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: The report’s headline return on equity was 13.1%, higher than 10.7% in Q1 but below 17.4% a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Net income increased 7% quarter on quarter and year on year to EUR 79.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Net interest income rose 5% from Q1 to EUR 62.5 million and was 8% higher than a year earlier, supported by loan growth and interest income that exceeded plan.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Net fee and commission income was broadly unchanged at EUR 14.6 million quarter on quarter but fell 6% year on year, mainly reflecting lower client activity.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Operating expenses declined 4% from Q1 to EUR 43.6 million, but were 8% above Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Operating profit consequently increased to EUR 35.4 million from EUR 28.1 million in Q1.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: This improvement was partly offset by EUR 5.8 million of impairment charges, compared with EUR 1.3 million in Q1 and a EUR 4.2 million reversal in Q2 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Management said the charges reflected forward-looking model provisions and a limited number of specific clients, while overall loan quality remained strong.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: For the first half of 2026, net profit was EUR 44.4 million, down 26% from EUR 59.9 million in the first half of 2025, while profit attributable to shareholders fell 25% to EUR 44.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Net operating income was broadly stable at EUR 152.6 million, but operating expenses increased 14% to EUR 89.2 million and impairment charges rose to EUR 7.1 million from EUR 1.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Income tax expense decreased 13% to EUR 12.1 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The loan portfolio grew 3% during the quarter and 15% year on year to EUR 5.77 billion, driven particularly by home and corporate lending.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Deposits fell 3% quarter on quarter to EUR 7.56 billion, primarily because of a deliberate reduction in platform deposits and lower financial-intermediary balances.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Capital adequacy was 20.8%, down from 21.7% in Q1 and 23.0% a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: LHV Pank generated EUR 24.3 million of Q2 profit, while LHV Bank earned EUR 1.4 million, Varahaldus EUR 0.4 million and Kindlustus EUR 0.8 million; Paytech recorded a EUR 0.3 million loss.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Insurance returned to profit as major losses and loss frequency declined, aided by better weather.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: During the quarter, the Bank completed its migration to a cloud-based core system, adopted product-based management, obtained Estonia’s first bank crypto-assets service-provider licence under MiCA, and advanced plans for international expansion.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Market conditions remained volatile amid geopolitical tensions and rising energy-price risks, while higher interest rates supported interest income and strong equity markets benefited asset-management activity.

evaluation.label: Generally yes

issues.description: S1 states consolidated net profit was EUR 24.7 million in Q2 2026, while S5 states net income increased to EUR 79.0 million. These figures represent different metrics (net profit vs. net income), but the summary does not clarify this distinction, creating an apparent contradiction for a reader unfamiliar with financial terminology.

evaluation.justification: The summary is generally coherent with logical relationships between financial metrics, clear organization, and minimal repetition. The primary issue is the potential confusion between 'consolidated net profit' (S1) and 'net income' (S5), which are presented without clarification that they are distinct measures. All other statements build logically on each other, with consistent comparisons across periods and clear explanations of drivers. The structure progresses from consolidated results to segment performance, operational metrics, and strategic updates, forming a coherent narrative. No other contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems are present.
